title: Port Conflict: EADDRINUSE in Globex Local and CI Environments
text:
Symptom: Globex service or test runner fails with 'Error: listen EADDRINUSE :::8080' or 'bind: address already in use' (Go). Port binding fails and service cannot start, causing health checks to fail and downstream services to report connection refused.

Root Cause: Parallel CI jobs using the same port on a shared runner; previous test suite did not release port after completion; Docker container from previous run still occupying host port; Globex gateway running on same port as a new microservice.

Diagnosis Steps:
1. In CI: check if parallel job matrix shares the same runner and port
2. Find occupying process: 'ss -tlnp | grep 8080' or 'netstat -tlnp | grep 8080'
3. Check Docker: 'docker ps | grep 8080'
4. For Go services: check for missing listener.Close() in service shutdown

Fix:
- Kill process: 'fuser -k 8080/tcp' (Linux) or 'kill $(lsof -t -i:8080)'
- For CI: use dynamic port allocation — set PORT=0 and let OS assign, then read assigned port from service startup log
- Docker: 'docker stop $(docker ps -q --filter publish=8080)'
- Globex microservices: each service has a default port in globex-services/config/ports.yaml — resolve conflicts there
- Use Globex service mesh (Envoy): all inter-service calls go through mesh, avoid direct port binding conflicts

Prevention: Assign dedicated port ranges per service in Globex port registry; use Docker Compose with fixed port mappings; integrate port-conflict-check in pre-commit hooks.
